newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB orders up on large projects.
newsitem.headline: ABB orders up on large projects.

text.p: Electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said a 16 percent increase in new orders in the first quarter of 1997 was driven by large projects and increased demand from emerging markets.
ABB also said its quarterly statement that orders for standard products and industrial goods were down slightly compared to last year, reflecting the second year of slowdown in Western Europe.
The order backlog at the end of March amounted to $34.2 billion, up one percent from the end of the 1996 first quarter.
New orders received in the first quarter orders rose 16 percent to $10.08 billion and expressed in local currencies the rise amounted to 22 percent.
ABB's net cash position at the end of March, however, was lower when compared with same period last year.
Additional orders from the Bakun, Malaysia, hydroelectric project were received in the first quarter, increasing orders at the Transmission and Distribution segment.
The Industrial and Building Systems segment also had higher orders, reflecting ABB's growing presence in oil, gas and petrochemical markets.
Orders also improved in the Power Generation segment and in transportation activities.
